review_notes: I read the whole target file, `PointSquareZeroPresentation.lean` (the simp lemmas and definitions it relies on), and the downstream fixtures that use `pointSquareZeroDelta` and `pointSquareZeroAlgEquiv`. The `@[simp]` lemmas stated in the target (`pointSquareZeroAlgEquiv_mk_some`, `_mk_none`, `_mk_C`, `_symm_delta`) look well oriented and have no obvious competing rules or loops. findings.excerpt: have hc (r : R) : algebraMap R (pointSquareZeroQuotient a) r = c r := by
findings.problem: The simp set has `pointSquareZero_algebraMap_C` for `algebraMap R[X] _ (Polynomial.C r)`, but no lemma puts `algebraMap R (pointSquareZeroQuotient a) r` into the same normal form `Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (C r)`. This proof therefore re-proves the identity locally. It uses `change`, a rewrite with `← pointSquareZero_algebraMap_C`, and `IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply`. Expressions mixing the `R`-algebra map and the `R[X]`-algebra map land in two different normal forms. The generators `pointSquareZero_linear` and `pointSquareZero_sq` are stated only in terms of `mk (C r)`.
findings.proposed_change: Move `hc` out as a public lemma, for example `pointSquareZero_algebraMap_R (a) (r : R) : algebraMap R (pointSquareZeroQuotient a) r = Ideal.Quotient.mk (pointSquareZeroIdeal a) (C r)`, and tag it `@[simp]`. The direction (algebraMap to `mk (C r)`) matches the existing `pointSquareZero_algebraMap_C`, so it cannot cycle. Then lines 62–67 become `simp only [map_sub, pointSquareZero_algebraMap_R]` followed by `ring`.
findings.benefit: Users and later proofs can normalise the `R`-algebra map into the same `mk (C r)` form that `pointSquareZero_linear` and `pointSquareZero_sq` use, without re-deriving it through the scalar tower. This removes the ad hoc local lemma and the `change`.

findings.problem: `pointSquareZeroDelta` is a plain `def`. No simp or characterising lemma describes it, such as `delta = lof … i (mk 1)`, its component `delta i j`, or `p • delta i = lof … i (mk p)`. Every consumer must unfold it with `rw [pointSquareZeroDelta, …]`, as at line 172 and in the local `hdelta` at lines 179–186. `hdelta` is exactly the missing smul-normal-form lemma. It is buried as a local `have` with a long explicit `fun k => R[X] ⧸ …` argument. Downstream fixtures also unfold the definition by hand (`simpa only [pointSquareZeroDelta, DirectSum.lof_apply, DFinsupp.zero_apply]`).
findings.proposed_change: State top-level lemmas next to `pointSquareZeroDelta` (or here): `pointSquareZeroDelta_smul (p : R[X]) : p • pointSquareZeroDelta a i = DirectSum.lof R[X] ι _ i (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ p)`. Add a component lemma, for example for `pointSquareZeroDelta a i j`, with an `if`/`Pi.single` right-hand side. Tag the smul lemma `@[simp]`: it reduces `•` on a basis element to the canonical `lof` form, and nothing rewrites back. Then lines 179–186 and the `rw [pointSquareZeroDelta, …]` at line 172 collapse into the simp-lemma call.
findings.benefit: A reader gets one canonical form for scalar multiples of the coordinate generators, and the delta-related goals in this file and in the downstream fixtures no longer need hand unfolding of the definition.

findings.excerpt: @[simp] private theorem pointSquareZeroSum_lof (a : ι → R) [DecidableEq ι] (i : ι)
findings.problem: The file marks `pointSquareZeroSum_lof` and `pointSquareZeroCoordinate_mk` `@[simp]` but then never lets simp use them. Every use is a manual `change … ; rw [pointSquareZeroSum_lof, …, pointSquareZeroCoordinate_mk, …]`, at lines 140, 172 and 197. Each use spells out the long `DirectSum.lof R[X] ι (fun k => R[X] ⧸ RingHom.ker …)` term. These lemmas are `private`, so they cannot serve as a simp interface for anyone outside the file. The `@[simp]` attribute is not exercised, and the `[DecidableEq ι]` argument has to be matched against `classical` instances in the proof. The simp interface for `pointSquareZeroSum` (the map `g`) is therefore half-built.
findings.proposed_change: Either drop `@[simp]` on these private lemmas and treat them as plain rewrite lemmas, or make the interface usable. For the second option, state a lemma for `pointSquareZeroSum` on `of`/`lof` with `algebraMap … * mk (X (some i))` as the normal form, together with the smul lemma from the previous finding. Then replace the `change … ; rw` blocks with `simp`. That also avoids the `classical` and `DecidableEq` instance mismatch.
findings.benefit: The simp annotations would match how the lemmas are actually used. The proofs of `hsingle`, `hleft` and `hright` would shrink and no longer depend on the exact `lof` and instance syntactic forms.
